```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo=FALSE, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE)
source("masem_workflow.R", local=TRUE)
source("utils.R", local=TRUE)
run <- params$run
data <- run$data
filters <- function(x) if(length(x)) paste(x,collapse=", ") else "All"
```

# Selection and estimation

Analysis run: **`r run$created`**.

Software: `r if(length(run$software)) paste(names(run$software),run$software,collapse="; ") else "Not recorded in this saved run"`.

- Variables (canonical codes): `r paste(run$selection$variables, collapse=", ")`.
- Age groups: `r filters(run$selection$ages)`.
- Publication years: `r filters(run$selection$years)`.
- Automatic exogenous covariances and endogenous residual covariances: `r run$auto_covariances`.

The model uses **one-stage MASEM (OSMASEM)**, fitted directly to the selected study-level correlation matrices and coded reference Ns. It does not fit a second-stage model to the exploratory pooled matrix. Sampling covariances use `acov="weighted"`; between-study heterogeneity is fixed at zero (`RE.type="Zero"`), and parameter intervals use the existing Wald-z setting. These settings have not been changed by this interface update.

The evidence base contains **`r length(unique(data$basic_info$paper_id))` articles** and **`r nrow(data$basic_info)` correlation matrices**. Matrices may share participants. Ns are reference sizes already coded in the database; their sum is not a count of unique people, and available N can vary by pair. Missing correlations are preserved. No automatic imputation, matrix repair, participant exclusion or replacement of Ns is performed.

# Data coverage

```{r variables, results='asis'}
report_table(data.frame(Code=run$selection$variables, Label=unname(run$labels[run$selection$variables])),caption="Selected variables")
```

```{r papers, results='asis'}
report_table(masem_sample_table(data),caption="Contributing matrices")
```

```{r coverage-k, results='asis'}
report_table(masem_named_matrix(data$K,run$labels),digits=0,caption="Contributing matrices per correlation (k)")
```

```{r coverage-n, results='asis'}
report_table(masem_named_matrix(data$N,run$labels),digits=0,caption="Sum of reference Ns per correlation")
```

Coverage warnings refer to distinct off-diagonal variable pairs. Fewer than three matrices or a reference-N sum below 1000 is an advisory warning, not an exclusion rule. Pairs without any reported correlation prevent estimation in this app.

```{r audit, results='asis'}
report_table(data$audit,caption="Matrix checks; source values retained")
```

# Effective model specification

The syntax below preserves the entered model, including supported fixed coefficients and parameter labels, and explicitly identifies any app-generated additions.

Fixed directed paths and variables without directed paths are supported. Fixed coefficients are retained in the syntax; the estimates table lists free parameters. Feedback structures are rejected because the current correlation-model calculation requires an acyclic model. Measurement models require explicit covariance specification with automatic covariances switched off.

```{r syntax, results='asis'}
cat("```text\n",run$syntax,"\n```\n",sep="")
```

# Model results

```{r diagnostics,results='asis'}
for(note in run$diagnostics) cat("\n\n",note,"\n",sep="")
if(isTRUE(run$summary$ChiDoF==0)) {
 cat("\n\nThis is a saturated model (df = 0). Global fit indices are not informative.\n")
} else {
 report_table(masem_fit_table(run),caption="Model fit")
}
```

Regression coefficients, loadings, covariances and variances are different model parameters; they are not all Pearson correlations. Intervals below are Wald 95% confidence intervals.

```{r parameters, results='asis'}
report_table(masem_parameters(run),caption="Model parameter estimates")
```

```{r technical,results='asis'}
cat('<details><summary>Model details: standard errors and Wald tests</summary>\n')
report_table(masem_parameters(run,details=TRUE))
cat('\n</details>\n')
```

## Residual variance and explained variance

R² is reported for endogenous variables where applicable as one minus the residual-to-total variance ratio. Total variance is obtained from the fitted RAM model. R² is not reported for feedback models or when the outcome residual correlates with a predictor. Negative or otherwise out-of-range values are retained and flagged rather than truncated.

```{r r2, results='asis'}
report_table(masem_r2(run),caption="Endogenous variables: residual variance and R²")
```

# Optional exploratory pooled matrix

The pooled matrix is a separate TSSEM calculation, not an input to the one-stage model above. It appears here only when computed successfully for the same data selection.

```{r pooled, results='asis'}
if(is.null(run$pooled)) {
 cat("No matching exploratory pooled matrix was calculated. The one-stage model does not require it.")
} else {
 matrix <- masem_named_matrix(run$pooled$matrix,run$labels)
 report_table(matrix,caption="Separate exploratory pooled correlations")
}
```

# Interpretation and reproducibility

This app supports exploratory synthesis of the curated SEB literature. Participant overlap, heterogeneous pair-specific Ns and limited coverage remain relevant limitations. Regression direction reflects the specified model and does not establish causation. The selected RDS or ZIP export preserves matrices, canonical variable names, reference Ns, filters and model syntax for reproduction.
